After an odd number of knight moves, the knight must be on a square of the opposite color from where it started. This is because each knight move changes the square's color.

The lower-left square is one color, so after 2009 moves the knight is on the other color. That color has 32 squares.

Every one of those squares is reachable:
- The knight graph on an 8×8 board is connected, and every square of the opposite color is at an odd distance from the start. That distance is at most 2009.
- Any extra moves can be spent in pairs by moving to a neighboring square and back, which adds 2 moves each time. So any odd shortest distance can be padded up to exactly 2009.

Therefore all 32 opposite-color squares can be reached.

ANSWER: 32
